state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. In a distance-time graph, a negative-sloping section represents Fido moving away from his home. Let's go through an example to clarify this concept.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so I think I get that the negative slope means Fido is moving back towards home instead of falling asleep. But how do we know he’s moving away from home when the line goes up? Does that mean he’s running away at first? I'm still a bit confused about how to tell the difference.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. In a distance-time graph, a positive slope represents Fido moving away from his home. Let's work through an example to help clarify this further.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that a positive slope means Fido is moving away from home, and a negative slope means he’s coming back. But what if the line is flat? Does that mean he’s just standing still? I'm still a bit confused about how to tell what Fido is doing at each part of the graph.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher makes a critical error in Turn 1 (stating negative slope means moving away when it actually means returning home), never addresses the student's specific confusion about rest vs. movement (horizontal sections), and simply tells answers rather than eliciting reasoning, though the student does show some improvement by Turn 4 in understanding slopes despite the teacher's initial error.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to explain directly and mentions working through examples (consistent with traditional teaching), they make a critical factual error in Turn 1 (stating negative slope means moving away when it means returning home) and provide repetitive, formulaic responses without actually working through the promised examples or adequately checking the student's understanding.
